name: Metrion
author: Metrion

sections.description:
WordPress native tracking plugin

Metrion natively tracks key ecommerce and lead interactions directly from WordPress and it’s most used ecommerce-plugin; Woo (Woocommerce).
Native tracking entails that data is collected by listening to the build-in triggers of WordPress and Woo instead of building layers of ‘technical trackings cosmetics’ on-top-off its foundations, making tracking unnecessarily complex and error-prone.
By directly integrating into WordPress you can skip expensive implementation costs and guarantee the highest level of data accuracy for growing your business.

Full Metrion Feature List

  • First party & server-side tracking
  • Advanced track-blocking detection
  • Consent Management Platform integrations
  • No data storage in cookies/browser storage before explicit consent (optional setting)
  • Event floodgating to prevent tracking before proper consent is given
  • Front-end event brokering
  • Server-side event brokering
  • Google Ads conversion tracking
  • Google Ads enhanced conversion tracking (Through Google Ads API)
  • Google Ads enhanced lead tracking
  • Google consent mode V2 (optional)
  • Google dynamic remarketing tracking for retail vertical
  • Meta Ads pixel implementation
  • Meta Conversion API integration (CAPI)
  • Meta Ads Advantage+ catalog ads tracking
  • Microsoft Ads conversion tracking
  • Microsoft Ads conversion enhancement through conversion uploading
  • Microsoft Ads consent mode
  • Microsoft Ads dynamic remarketing list functionality
  • Google Analytics 4 sever-side

External services

This plugin connects to multiple external APIs based on the configured settings within your Metrion plugin. No data is shared to other external services (aside from Metrion) when using Metrion’s default settings. Data collection can be limited through the plugin’s settings and its integrations with consent management platforms like Cookiebot, Cookieyes, etc.

Metrion tracking API

When tracking of no external marketing channels is activated/enabled, only Metrion’s tracking API endpoints are used. This tracking API is used for collecting a fixed set of user interactions on your website as of this release:
– Visit
– Page view
– Product view
– Product list view
– Search result list view
– Add to cart
– Cart view
– Checkout start
– Purchase
– Form submits
When a user is identified with data like an email address, phone number, this data can be included with each interaction based on the consent configurations within Metrion.
This data is temporarily stored for conversion attribution purposes. Read more about our terms of use and privacy policy.

Google Ads Tracking

When Google Ads tracking is activated, this plugin loads and connects with to Google Ads’ tracking pixels and APIs. Based on the Google Ads settings in Metrion’s, the user interaction data can be shared with Google Ads.

Read more about our terms of use and privacy policy.

Meta Ads Tracking

When Meta Ads tracking is activated, this plugin loads and connects with to Meta Ads’ tracking pixels and APIs. Based on the Meta Ads settings in Metrion’s, the user interaction data can be shared with Meta Ads.

Read more about our terms of use and privacy policy.

Microsoft Ads Tracking

When Microsoft Ads tracking is activated, this plugin loads and connects with to Microsoft Ads’ tracking pixels and APIs. Based on the Microsoft Ads settings in Metrion’s, the user interaction data can be shared with Microsoft Ads.

Read more about our terms of use and privacy policy.
sections.installation:
1. Install the Metrion plugin via the WordPress.org plugin repository or by uploading the files to your server. (See instructions on how to install a WordPress plugin)
  2. Activate Metrion.
  3. Navigate to settings > Metrion in your admin menu and configurate your Metrion plugin to meet your tracking needs.
  4. Need help? Contact the Metrion team for implementation support!
